title: Dual Genetic Risk in a Couple with Prior Vasectomy and Advanced Maternal Age: Indication for Simultaneous PGT-A and PGT-M
content: Background: Preconception expanded carrier screening (ECS) and preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) have transformed reproductive medicine. Couples presenting simultaneously with advanced maternal age (AMA), diminished ovarian reserve (DOR), post-vasectomy obstructive azoospermia, and shared carrier status for several autosomal recessive disorders pose a distinct management challenge, and few reviews address these factors in an integrated way. Objective: To review the current evidence on integrated reproductive decision-making for couples with this combination of factors, illustrated by a representative clinical case. Methods: We conducted a narrative review of the recent literature on ECS, PGT-A/PGT-M, surgical sperm retrieval, and donor oocyte IVF. To contextualize the literature on genetic risk, a topic search was performed in Web of Science on 15 September 2026 using the terms "chromosomal disorders" AND "genetic disorders" AND "multiple genetic disorders". The search returned 13,719 documents for "chromosomal disorders", 6,410 after adding "genetic disorders", and 962 after adding "multiple genetic disorders". No other database was searched using these terms. Additional articles and professional society guidelines were identified through manual searches and screening of reference lists. We then present a case report of one couple. Results: The literature indicates that autologous IVF with testicular fine needle aspiration (FNA) and concurrent PGT-A/PGT-M can identify unaffected euploid embryos without reducing per-embryo euploidy relative to PGT-A alone. However, cumulative success is limited by age-related aneuploidy and low ovarian reserve. IVF with donated oocytes and genetic matching, avoids age-related aneuploidy and the need for PGT-M. In the present case report, both partners were heterozygous carriers of variants in MEFV (familial Mediterranean fever) and HFE (hereditary hemochromatosis type 1). This corresponds to a theoretical Mendelian risk of 43.75% per pregnancy for at least one condition and 6.25% for both, before accounting for incomplete penetrance. The female partner’s ovarian reserve was low (AMH 0.71 ng/mL). Conclusions: Management of couples with genetic risk and complex reproductive factors should be strictly individualized. Multidisciplinary counseling that integrates genetic prognosis, expected embryo yield, sperm retrieval strategy, and ethical considerations is essential to support informed decision-making.
